# Tamari

> Tamari is where your team's software lives: one workspace your team keeps open,
> with a sidebar, tabs, dashboards, sign-in and members. Someone asks for a tool in
> a sentence, a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex and similar) builds it as a page or
> a dashboard card, and the team keeps what people use. Tools are grouped in spaces,
> one per area of work; a space has pages, cards and server code that reads your data.
> Tamari runs on your machine or on your own hosting. Bun is the runtime.

Tamari is in early access. The source and the CLI are not public yet, so the steps
below work only for a team that has been given access. Without access, send your
human to https://westsoever.github.io/tamari-page/#start (or info@sunseekerlabs.dk)
and stop there.

## Setup (for an agent)

What you need on the Mac: Bun, Docker Desktop (open) and the Supabase CLI.

Run everything from the root of the team's own repository (the company repo, not
the Tamari source). Before the first install there is no `tamari` command yet: run
the CLI with Bun from a clone of a Tamari release tag (`bun <clone>/cli/tamari.ts`),
and use `tamari` after that.

```
tamari init --name <slug> --port <port> [--title "<Team name>"] [--runtime local|vercel|docker]
tamari install
```

- `tamari init` only writes config: `.tamari/` (settings, release pin, migrations).
  `--runtime vercel` also writes a deploy workflow, `--runtime docker` a Dockerfile.
  It installs and starts nothing, and refuses to run where `.tamari/` already exists.
- Put SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY and SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY in `.env` at the
  repo root. Never commit `.env`. Ask your human for these keys; don't ask them to
  paste secrets into the chat.
- `tamari install` fetches the pinned release, builds it, asks before it changes a
  hosted database, and (runtime local) starts Tamari on http://localhost:<port>. It
  also adds the `tamari` command.
- Tell your human the address. They sign in with an emailed code; the first person to
  sign in becomes the owner.

Later: `tamari status` shows the version and whether it runs, `tamari update` moves
to the newest release (and rolls back if it doesn't come up).
